$comment: Registry of external factual claims (regulatory citations + statistics) used in marketing emails, site copy, and course content. Every regulatory token or sourced statistic in a scanned surface must be covered by an entry here, and every entry has a reviewBy date. scripts/check-claims.mjs enforces both in CI. Re-verify claims before their reviewBy date (see docs: monthly re-verification routine).

claims.claim: SR 26-2 is the revised interagency guidance on model risk management (FRB/OCC/FDIC, April 17, 2026); it supersedes SR 11-7. Non-binding; generative and agentic AI are outside its formal scope while agencies gather input.
SR 11-7 (2011) may be mentioned only as history: as the guidance SR 26-2 superseded. It must not appear as a standing anchor on its own.
The AIEOG AI Lexicon (US Treasury, FBIIC, FSSCC) was released February 19, 2026 and defines shared AI terms for the financial sector, including 'AI use case inventory'. Non-binding.
Treasury also released the Financial Services AI Risk Management Framework (FS AI RMF) in February 2026 alongside the Lexicon. Non-binding.
Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management (88 FR 37920, June 2023) remains current guidance.

GAO-25-107197 (May 2025) found no comprehensive AI-specific banking regulation exists; oversight works through extensions of existing frameworks. Still accurate after SR 26-2 (which is model-risk guidance, non-binding, and excludes generative AI).

55% of FIs have no AI governance framework; 57% report team-level skill gaps; 48% say leadership lacks clarity on AI's business impact (Gartner Peer Community data, via Jack Henry, 2025). A 2026 Jack Henry Strategy Benchmark now exists; refresh or knowingly retain the 2025 citation.
claims.source: Jack Henry 'Getting Started in AI' (2025), citing Gartner Peer Community

claims.claim: 66% of banks are discussing AI budget allocation (Bank Director 2024 Technology Survey, via Jack Henry). Figure still circulating and accurate as cited in Aug 2026; Bank Director 2026 Risk / Compensation surveys offer fresher numbers.
~56.0% is the industry-wide efficiency ratio (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, Q1 2026; was 55.7% at Q4 2025). Refresh each QBP release.
claims.source: FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile Q1 2026 / CEIC

claims.claim: ~65% is the long-run median efficiency ratio for community banks (FDIC data via CEIC, 1992-2025). Note: cohort medians improved 4-7 points between 1Q24 and 1Q26, so this long-run figure is drifting from current-period medians.
84% of consumers would likely switch to a bank providing timely, relevant AI-driven financial advice (Personetics global survey, Feb 2025, via Apiture).
claims.source: Personetics 'Understanding Consumer Demand in the AI-Banking Era'

claims.claim: 76% of consumers are likely to switch banks for one that better fits their needs (Motley Fool Money survey via Pollfish, Jan 2024; up from 52% in 2020). Apiture and the site's copy render this as 'would switch FIs for a better digital experience' — acceptable gloss given the survey's digital-banking-trends context. Verified against the fool.com primary source 2026-09-30.
claims.source: The Motley Fool 'Online Banking Trends and Consumer Priorities' (via Apiture)

claims.claim: SR 21-8 (April 2021) is the interagency statement on model risk management for bank systems supporting BSA/AML compliance; SR 26-2 supersedes it where applicable.

The CSBS Artificial Intelligence Supervisory Framework (released September 16, 2026) is a discretionary resource for state examiners reviewing AI use at state-chartered banks and state-licensed nonbank financial institutions. It creates no new legal requirements; each state decides how to use it. Its Core Examiner Guide includes initial scoping questions, a document request list, and procedures covering governance/oversight, the AI inventory and use cases, and generative AI. Built on the NIST AI RMF, the FS AI RMF, and Treasury's AI Lexicon.
ECOA / Regulation B govern fair lending, including adverse action requirements as applied to AI-assisted credit decisions.
On May 12, 2025 the CFPB withdrew 67 guidance documents, including the May 2024 BNPL interpretive rule (89 FR 47068). The notice says the withdrawal is not necessarily final.
claims.source: CFPB, Interpretive Rules, Policy Statements, and Advisory Opinions; Withdrawal (Federal Register document 2025-08286)

claims.claim: Congress overturned the CFPB's 2024 overdraft rule for very large financial institutions in 2025 under the Congressional Review Act (S.J.Res. 18, Public Law 119-10); the rule never took effect.
claims.source: Congress.gov, S.J.Res.18 (119th Congress) and CRS Insight IN12513

claims.claim: The Federal Reserve's SR 26-2 transmittal states the letter is expected to be most relevant to banking organizations with over $30 billion in total assets regulated by the Federal Reserve; it notes model risk management practices appropriately vary with risk profile and model usage.

The 2023 interagency third-party guidance (Fed, FDIC, OCC) organizes risk management around a five-stage life cycle: planning; due diligence and third-party selection; contract negotiation; ongoing monitoring; termination. Oversight is to be commensurate with the organization's size, complexity, and risk profile and the nature of the relationship.

Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9(b)(2): the statement of reasons for adverse action must be specific and indicate the principal reason(s); statements that the action was based on internal standards or policies, or on failure to achieve a qualifying score, are insufficient.

GAO-25-107197 (May 19, 2025) reports that NCUA lacks the authority to examine technology service providers despite credit unions' increasing reliance on them for AI-driven services, and reiterates a 2015 recommendation that Congress grant that authority.
match: authority to examine technology service providers

claims.claim: The CSBS AI Supervisory Framework includes an AI Use Case Risk Tiering Worksheet, described as an optional industry tool to support a risk-based assessment of individual AI use cases, alongside the Core Examiner Guide and an Examiner Work Program.

On September 15, 2026 the OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, and NCUA proposed third-party risk management guidance (FR Doc. 2026-18859) that would rescind and replace existing guidance; comments due November 16, 2026. Components: risk identification and assessment; risk oversight (due diligence and selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination); residual risk acceptance; governance.

SR 26-2 attachment: models at banking organizations with total assets of $30 billion or less are typically subject to internal practices appropriate for their size, and generally excluding them from the guidance is consistent with a tailored supervisory approach; it may still be relevant to smaller organizations with significant model risk exposure.
claims.source: Federal Reserve, SR 26-2 attachment (Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management)

claims.claim: The 2026 model risk guidance states generative AI and agentic AI models are novel and rapidly evolving and are not within its scope; the OCC, Federal Reserve, and FDIC plan a request for information on model risk management including banks' use of generative and agentic AI.
